formats.key: UserDecryptRequestVerification(address userAddress,bytes publicKey,address[] allowedContracts,uint256 startTimestamp,uint256 durationSeconds,bytes extraData)
effects: The signer lets the Zama KMS re-encrypt the signer's confidential values under `publicKey`. Whoever holds the matching private key can read them.
The permission covers only the ciphertext handles of the contracts in `allowedContracts`.
The permission starts at `startTimestamp` and lasts `durationSeconds`.
`userAddress` names the account whose data is decrypted, which is normally the signer. No token moves, and no allowance or position changes.
formats.shown: The screen says "Authorize decryption of your confidential data" and "Authorize <userAddress> to decrypt for <contract> for 240:00:00". It shows the requesting account, the authorized contracts, a start date and a duration, and hides the public key and the extra data.

findings.title: UserDecryptRequestVerification hides publicKey, which decides who can read the decrypted data.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json, format UserDecryptRequestVerification: field {"path": "publicKey", "label": "Public key", "format": "raw", "visible": "never"}. Cases 0 and 1 show no public key. The holder of the matching private key reads the re-encrypted values. No asset moves.
findings.fix: Make `publicKey` visible with the label "Data revealed to holder of key". Or change the intent to say the data is revealed to the app's session key. Keep it out of interpolatedIntent.

findings.title: UserDecryptRequestVerification interpolatedIntent reads as if a third party gets decryption rights.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json interpolatedIntent "Authorize {userAddress} to decrypt for {allowedContracts.[]} for {durationSeconds}". Case 0 renders "Authorize 0x7099…79C8 to decrypt for 0x3C44…93BC for 240:00:00". userAddress is the account whose data is decrypted, normally the signer, and is labelled "Requesting account".
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to "Allow decryption of your data from {allowedContracts.[]} for {durationSeconds}".

findings.title: UserDecryptRequestVerification shows a 10-day duration as '240:00:00', which is hard to read.
findings.evidence: Field durationSeconds, format "duration". Case 0 shows "Valid for: 240:00:00" for 864000 seconds. The spec's duration format renders HH:MM:SS, and no format shows days or an end date.

findings.title: UserDecryptRequestVerification hides extraData, and its meaning cannot be checked without source.
findings.evidence: Field {"path": "extraData", "format": "raw", "visible": "never"}. Cases 0 and 1 use "0x". The KMS consumes it, and it moves no assets.

findings.title: UserDecryptRequestVerification tests use only one allowed contract, so the multi-contract rendering is untested.
findings.evidence: Cases 0 and 1 both use "allowedContracts": ["0x3C44…93BC"]. They differ only in chain. No test shows how the sentence renders several contracts.
findings.fix: Add a case with two or more allowedContracts.

couldNotCheck: The verifying contract 1:0x0f6024a97684f7d90ddb0faad79cb15f2c888d24 has no verified source and no ABI. The EIP-712 domain (name "Decryption", version "1") and the struct type string could not be checked against the contract.

The Sepolia deployment 11155111:0x5D8BD78e2ea6bbE41f26dFe9fdaEAa349e077478 has no contract data in the directory. In Zama's design the Decryption contract may sit on the Gateway chain, with the off-chain KMS checking signatures. So the binding and the meaning of userAddress and extraData could not be confirmed.
